summary:
ORBITWISE: Mission Architect
An Interactive Space Mission Design and Simulation Game

ORBITWISE: Mission Architect is an interactive web-based educational game developed to make space mission planning engaging and accessible. Users can design a simulated Mars mission by selecting spacecraft power systems, scientific instruments, mission duration, launch vehicle, destination, orbit profile, and communication systems.

The application calculates illustrative estimates for mission budget, spacecraft mass, power reserve, scientific return, risk, and overall readiness. It also includes a Mission Doctor that provides recommendations, interactive mission events that challenge users to make decisions, a mission comparison feature, and downloadable mission reports.

ORBITWISE addresses the challenge of teaching technology through interactive learning. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, users can experiment with engineering choices, understand resource constraints, and observe how decisions affect mission outcomes.

The project is important because it introduces complex space mission concepts in a beginner-friendly format, encouraging scientific curiosity, critical thinking, and problem-solving. It provides an accessible starting point for learning about spacecraft design and mission planning through hands-on simulation.
details:
ORBITWISE: Mission Architect

Project Description

ORBITWISE: Mission Architect is an interactive, NASA-inspired educational web application that helps users design, configure, and simulate space missions to Mars. It allows users to understand how different mission decisions affect spacecraft performance, cost, power, risk, and scientific return.

How does it work?

Users can configure a spacecraft by selecting a mission name, power system, mission priority, scientific instruments, and mission duration. They can choose between solar arrays and radioisotope thermoelectric generator (RTG) nuclear power, and select equipment such as high-resolution cameras, subsurface radar, sample analysis laboratories, and autonomous navigation systems.

After configuring the mission, users can run a simulation to explore estimated mission readiness, budget, power reserve, risk index, and science return. The Mission Doctor provides suggestions to improve the configuration. The Contingency Lab introduces unexpected events, such as a solar dust storm, encouraging users to consider suitable responses. The Engineering Constraints section explores payload mass, launch capacity, destination, communications, and orbital planning. Users can also compare their mission design with an alternative and export a mission report.

What are its benefits?

  • Makes space mission planning easier to understand through interactive simulations.
  • Demonstrates the trade-offs between mission cost, safety, power, and scientific objectives.
  • Encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making.
  • Introduces students to spacecraft systems, Mars exploration, and engineering constraints.
  • Provides a practical and engaging learning experience without requiring physical spacecraft hardware.

What is the intended impact?

The project's goal is to make space exploration and mission engineering more accessible to students and space enthusiasts. It aims to encourage interest in aerospace engineering, computer science, and planetary science while helping users understand the complexity of planning missions to Mars. It also supports science education and innovation by turning abstract engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience.

Tools, programming languages, and software used

  • Frontend: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
  • Development environment: Web browser and code editor
  • Deployment: GitHub Pages
  • Application type: Interactive web-based educational simulation

How is the project creative?

ORBITWISE combines spacecraft configuration, mission analysis, AI-inspired recommendations, emergency scenario exploration, and design comparison in one interactive dashboard. Instead of simply presenting information about Mars, it allows users to make decisions and explore their consequences. The Mission Doctor and Contingency Lab make the experience more engaging by introducing recommendations and unexpected mission challenges.

What factors did the team consider?

The project considers mission cost, power availability, scientific objectives, spacecraft mass, launch capacity, communications coverage, mission duration, operational risk, and unexpected environmental events. The interface is designed to help users compare competing priorities and understand why a mission design must balance scientific value with safety and available resources.

Project limitation

ORBITWISE is an educational simulation. Its cost, power, readiness, risk, and event outcomes are simplified illustrative estimates, not official NASA engineering predictions. The current version does not use live NASA API data.

Live project: https://fathimathujumanao-ui.github
